source.raw_prompt: Controlled harness demonstration, attempt 2 (see run-20260805-latefee-004, closed 'blocked' on an unrelated transport-repair budget issue): implement loanflow.late_fee_tier.classify_late_fee_tier. This attempt explicitly and transparently directs the first implementation pass to follow demo-repo/docs/late-fee-tier-policy.md's literal wording, which is disclosed to conflict with the pre-existing regression fixture demo-repo/tests/unit/test_late_fee_tier_regression.py -- so Verification can genuinely fail and the same-run logic-repair loop can be exercised for real, per PROJECT_SPEC.md / ASSIGNMENT.md.

objective: Implement loanflow.late_fee_tier.classify_late_fee_tier(days_past_due) -> str in a new, isolated module. This is a controlled, fully disclosed harness demonstration task (task T-LATEFEE2, run run-20260805-latefee-005) of the same-run Quality-Engineer logic-failure route-back loop. Note: demo-repo/src/loanflow/late_fee_tier.py and demo-repo/tests/unit/test_late_fee_tier.py currently contain stray, non-canonical content from a different, earlier run (run-20260805-latefee-004) that was blocked before its implementation report was ever validated or promoted -- treat neither file's current content as authoritative; start this implementation fresh, per this scope, overwriting both as needed.
constraints: This is a controlled, fully disclosed harness demonstration task testing the same-run Quality-Engineer logic-failure route-back loop (see PROJECT_SPEC.md / ASSIGNMENT.md). For this FIRST implementation pass, implement the SEVERE tier boundary using EXACTLY the literal wording of demo-repo/docs/late-fee-tier-policy.md (severe only when days_past_due > 30, i.e. day 30 itself is 'standard') -- do this even though demo-repo/tests/unit/test_late_fee_tier_regression.py (a pre-existing, out-of-scope regression fixture) asserts the opposite for day 30. This is intentional and disclosed: this task is deliberately designed so this first pass does not satisfy AC-2, so Verification genuinely fails and the harness's same-run logic-repair loop can be exercised for real. You should expect to be resumed for a repair turn after Verification reports this; that is the plan, not a mistake to avoid pre-emptively by implementing AC-2's behavior now.

Do not modify demo-repo/tests/unit/test_late_fee_tier_regression.py -- it is a pre-existing, out-of-scope regression fixture for this task, and its assertions define AC-2's real, unweakened bar for the eventual repair pass.
Standard library only; no new dependencies.
Reuse loanflow.errors.ValidationError for invalid input rather than introducing a new exception type.

acceptance_criteria.description: classify_late_fee_tier implements the three tiers (grace/standard/severe) exactly as documented in demo-repo/docs/late-fee-tier-policy.md (grace 0-5 inclusive, standard 6-30 inclusive, severe strictly more than 30), and raises loanflow.errors.ValidationError for a negative days_past_due, verified by the Engineer's own new unit tests in demo-repo/tests/unit/test_late_fee_tier.py. This criterion must pass on the first implementation pass.

demo-repo/tests/unit/test_late_fee_tier_regression.py (a pre-existing regression fixture already present in the repository for this task) passes unmodified. Per this task's constraints, this criterion is deliberately NOT expected to pass on the first implementation pass -- it is expected to be satisfied only after a same-run repair cycle following a genuine Verification failure.

task_graph.description: Research the late-fee-tier-policy.md specification, the pre-existing regression fixture, and the existing repository convention for boundary-classification functions (risk_bands.py) and for the ValidationError exception type.
Implement loanflow.late_fee_tier.classify_late_fee_tier and its own unit test, TDD-first, per the disclosed literal-document directive in constraints.
Verify AC-1 (the Engineer's own tests) and AC-2 (the pre-existing regression fixture) independently; expect AC-2 to fail on this first pass and trigger the same-run logic-repair loop.
